newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bandai says Sega merger may fall behind schedule.
newsitem.headline: Bandai says Sega merger may fall behind schedule.

text.p: Bandai Co Ltd said the company's planned merger with Sega Enterprises Ltd may not be completed by October 1 as scheduled.

A company spokeswoman on Wednesday confirmed a comment by Bandai president Makoto Yamashina in a recent interview with the Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun, in which he indicated the merger could fall behind schedule.
"It is not that we are expecting the merger to be delayed, but rules on how to operate the new company are being hammered out very carefully," the spokeswoman said.
A spokesman for Sega said his company did not expect any delays in the merger, although he said that the two companies had an enormous number of items to work out before it was completed.
"We must prepare to become a truly unified company in order to survive the rapid changes in our industry," he said.

The Bandai spokeswoman said top executives from Bandai, Sega and CSK Corp, which is to hold 20 percent in the new company, have been discussing various matters including the assignment of responsibilities for boosting the firms' sagging profitability.
Analysts have said that, after January's announcement of the merger plan, one of the biggest hurdles facing the two companies was the extreme contrast in their corporate cultures.

"While Sega was owned by a foreign company, Bandai is a firm of long standing in Japan. It will not be easy to harmonise those companies' considerably different cultures," said Mitsuko Morita, analyst at Morgan Stanley Japan Ltd.
Toy maker Bandai and game-machine manufacturer Sega said in January they would merge on October 1 to build what they said would be a "formidable force" in the media entertainment business.
Sega's president Hayao Nakayama said at that time that the new company would have annual sales of 600 billion yen.
